title: Capital: Tokyo
d: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.
definition: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.
description: Tokyo is the capital of Japan: the seat of government and usually the cultural and economic heart. Capitals concentrate the nation's story — its museums, monuments, markets, and neighborhoods. Visitors should start here: a capital city teaches in days what books take weeks to explain.

title: Climate
description: The climate of Japan: temperate. Climate dictates the wardrobe, the harvest calendar, the festivals, and the architecture — life bends around weather everywhere. Travelers should check the seasons: the same country can feel like two different places between its wet and dry, hot and cold months.

title: Government
description: Japan is governed as a constitutional monarchy. The system of government shapes daily life through laws, services, and the citizen's relationship to the state. Its modern form dates to 660 BC (legendary); modern 1868 — and like all governments, it continues to evolve with its people.

title: Independence and statehood
description: Statehood in Japan: 660 BC (legendary); modern 1868. National days, flags, and anthems all trace to the moment of independence or founding — the story every schoolchild learns. Understanding it explains the country's pride, its holidays, and often its friendships and rivalries.

title: Languages
description: Language in Japan: Japanese. Language carries the culture's humor, proverbs, and worldview — learning even greetings opens doors that stay closed to outsiders. Multilingual countries code-switch daily; visitors who try the local tongue are repaid with warmth.

title: Currency and money
description: Money in Japan: the Japanese yen. Travelers should learn the denominations, the tipping customs, and whether cards or cash rule daily life. Exchange rates move, but the habit of checking prices in local terms keeps budgets honest.
